issues.detail: Covers configuration and migration steps but gives little troubleshooting guidance for common failures such as failed dependency pre-bundling, proxy errors, or CommonJS interop breakage beyond one legacy flag.

scenarios.name: cra-to-vite-migration
scenarios.rationale: Both cover installing Vite and the plugin, removing react-scripts, renaming env vars to VITE_* with import.meta.env, and moving index.html with a module script tag; B also supplies the requested vite.config.ts with the '@' alias, whereas A gives a vite.config.js with no alias, only mentioning resolve.alias in passing.

scenarios.name: vendor-chunks-sourcemaps-vite8
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric directly (sourcemap: true, rolldownOptions codeSplitting groups with /node_modules/ vendor, warning about not serving maps publicly if private), while B uses sourcemap: 'hidden' instead of true, hedges about codeSplitting vs advancedChunks, though it does cover not shipping maps and adds the Sentry plugin.

scenarios.name: dev-proxy-and-typed-env
scenarios.rationale: Both cover proxy, alias, ImportMetaEnv in vite-env.d.ts, import.meta.env usage, restart note and no-secrets warning; B adds changeOrigin, a __dirname fallback, separate dev and prod env files and a usage snippet, while A is more concise and uses the ESM-safe alias by default, so B is slightly more complete.
